result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You had a rheumatology review on 17 September 2026. The letter tells you to keep taking your current medicines. It also tells you to keep having blood tests at your GP (family doctor) surgery. Your next rheumatology review is in 6 months.

## What you need to do
1. Keep taking your current medicines.
2. Keep having blood tests every 3 months at your GP (family doctor) surgery.
3. Take methotrexate only once a week. Do not take it every day.
4. Take ibuprofen only when you need it for joint pain. Take it with food.

## Dates and medicines
- 17 September 2026: your rheumatology review. It has already happened.
- Every 3 months: blood tests at your GP surgery.
- In 6 months: your next rheumatology review. The letter gives no exact date.

Medicines (no changes. Continue all three):
- Methotrexate: 15 milligrams, once a WEEK, on Mondays.
- Folic acid: 5 milligrams, once a week, on Thursdays.
- Ibuprofen: 400 milligrams, up to 3 times a day with food, when needed for joint pain.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What does rheumatology mean?
- When will I get the date for my next review?
- Who will book my blood tests?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.
